notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, as the county reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
Public schools are run by separate school districts, so they are not included.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Payments to other governments ($18,410,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.

Political money counts itemized cash contributions from businesses, unions and political committees to Larimer County candidates whose committee names a county office, reported to the Secretary of State's TRACER since 2023. Committees whose names do not show the office are left out, so this is a floor. Individuals, LLC members, in-kind gifts and party and candidate committees are not counted.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-20. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Colorado yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Third-party investigative platform
redFlags.detail: The Larimer District Attorney received an enterprise license for LexisNexis' Accurint Virtual Crime Center through its membership in the Colorado Information Sharing Consortium.

Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Cameras: 19 license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Fort Collins's borders in OpenStreetMap (18 made by Flock Safety), not counting cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies. Flock cameras count as a red flag whoever runs them. Other brands count only when the government is the recorded operator, since many have no operator recorded.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-20. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for Colorado yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Flock camera network
redFlags.detail: 18 Flock Safety license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Fort Collins's borders in OpenStreetMap. Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is not recorded; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.
